USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the current tariff posture without new escalation. The US has already deployed tariffs on ~$250B of Chinese imports and secured a scheduled G-20 meeting between Trump and Xi in November. Escalating further now risks deepening the market correction and undermining the diplomatic opening. Conceding would squander leverage while China's economy is under pressure.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to US interests is moderate (0.2), driven by the following:

(a) The US economy remains fundamentally strong — consumer sentiment at 98.6 (Oct), industrial production at 104.0 (up 1.5% over the period), and unemployment near cycle lows. The tariff costs have not yet materially damaged the real economy.

(b) However, the October market selloff is a clear warning signal. The Dow dropped 800+ points on Oct 10 (worst day since Feb), the S&P 500 fell 5%+ from peaks, and the Nasdaq declined ~10%. Multiple sources attribute this directly to trade war fears compounding with rising rates (Fed funds up to 2.19%, 10Y yield at 3.19%). Corporate bond spreads (Baa at 5.07%) are rising, signaling credit stress.

(c) The IMF downgraded global growth forecasts by 0.2pp specifically citing trade measures. Companies including Tiffany and Delphi Technologies have warned of tariff-related profit hits. The Semiconductor Industry Association noted US chip tariffs hurt US firms more than Chinese ones since chips fabricated in the US get re-exported from China.

(d) China is under greater strain — their stock index entered bear market territory and the yuan weakened significantly — which gives the US negotiating leverage. The White House appears to believe it is winning the trade war. But China has matched every escalation tit-for-tat and shows no sign of capitulating on structural IP/tech-transfer issues.

(e) The Trump-Xi G-20 meeting in November is the critical near-term event. Escalating before that meeting would undermine the diplomatic channel. The current tariff level (List 3 at 10%, rising to 25% Jan 1) already provides significant pressure. No new action is needed to maintain leverage.

(f) The Nov 6 midterm elections create domestic political incentive to appear tough, but also create risk if market volatility worsens. Holding steady projects strength without inviting further market disruption.
